stability: Every entry documents an INLINE result shape (this target starts no executions and emits no outputs[] file list — kind inline throughout, the tts/hybrid-search precedent). The field names and nesting shown in each example are stable API; removing or renaming any is a breaking change requiring a TOOL_VERSION bump and a changelog note here. The S3 pair under _promptregistry/{category}/{version}/ (source.md + artifact.json) is readable directly but the TOOLS are the contract surface; anything else under _promptregistry/ is internal and may change without notice.

prompt-artifact.description: get_prompt's result: the full parsed artifact plus source_s3uri — everything prompt_render needs, plus stage so a caller can refuse to bind a dev prompt into a prod pipeline

example.system: You are an expert media content analyst...

prompt-artifact.notes: version is OPTIONAL on get_prompt and resolves to `default`; a NAMED missing version is PROMPT_NOT_FOUND, never a silent fallback. Content fields (system, user_template, variables, source_md5) are immutable for the life of the version; only stage/deprecated/promoted_at/deprecated_at ever change. `variables` is the pre-declared token list prompt_render substitutes — consumers never parse the {{...}} grammar themselves.

put-result.description: put_prompt's result: the saved identity plus the vocabulary lint — warnings are advisory and NEVER block a save
put-result.notes: stage defaults to dev; version `default` is forced to prod (a `message` field says so when it happens). Refusals: VERSION_EXISTS (versions are immutable — an edit is a new version name; dev/test names can be freed with delete_prompt), INVALID_PROMPT (the parse error verbatim), PROMPT_TOO_LARGE (~1 MB paste-accident bound), INVALID_PARAMETER.

list-entry.description: list_prompts' result: categories with per-version lifecycle metadata (no template bodies — get_prompt fetches those)
list-entry.notes: category is optional; absent lists every category. Per-version metadata costs one GET each — acceptable at registry scale and the documented price of keeping lifecycle metadata in the artifact.

lifecycle-result.description: promote_prompt / delete_prompt / deprecate_prompt results — small identity echoes with the state that changed, idempotent where retries must not error
lifecycle-result.notes: promote is a one-way ratchet (dev -> test -> prod); already-at-or-beyond-target returns success with a `message` (covers `default`, born prod, with no special case). delete returns {deleted: true, stage_was, message} and refuses prod (PROD_UNDELETABLE) — deprecate instead. deprecate returns {deprecated: true, deprecated_at}, is idempotent-with-message, and refuses `default` (DEFAULT_PROTECTED). All refusals are {error: true, errorCode, message}.
